situation:
You are the brand manager for WESTGATE TERIYAKI COMPANY, a chain of twenty-four rice bowl restaurants. After two years of losses the owners brought in a new president (judge), and the president (judge) has promised the owners the chain will stop losing money this year. You have been asked for a recommendation on price.

The signature chicken teriyaki bowl sells for nine dollars and has not changed price in four years. It is printed at the top of every menu board and it is what most first-time customers order. Chicken, rice and produce all cost more than they did, and the bowl now earns less than any other item on the board.

A study of two years of transaction data says a one-dollar increase on the bowl would move very few customers. The shift leaders and the long-tenured crew disagree. They face the regulars three times a week, and they say the bowl is why those customers come and that they will notice the day the board changes.

Raising the bowl a dollar across all twenty-four restaurants recovers the margin the data promises, but if the crew are right the chain loses its most frequent customers and the crew stop trusting the turnaround. Holding the price and charging separately for extra sauce, with a larger bowl at a higher price, recovers less margin, delays the promise made to the owners, and slows service at the counter.

The president (judge) wants your recommendation on what the chain should do with the bowl price, and on how the decision should be explained to the crew. You will present in the office at the support center. The president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the president's questions, the president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of WESTGATE TERIYAKI COMPANY. Business background is the same as the situation above. You want the brand manager to recommend what the chain does with the price of the signature chicken teriyaki bowl, and to say how the decision gets explained to the shift leaders and the crew who disagree with it.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: Six months from now, how will we know whether this worked?
What would tell us we got it wrong?
